aciemque: aciēs, -ēī (f.) — battle line, army in array (acc. sg. + -que)
adceperit: accipiō (adc-), -ere, -cēpī, -ceptum — to receive, accept, take up (3rd sg. pf. subj., in a relative clause of cause)
adcinxerat: accingō (adc-), -ere, -cīnxī, -cīnctum — to gird on, buckle to (3rd sg. plpf. act.; laterī ensem, 'had buckled a sword to his side')
adcommoda: accommodus (adc-), -a, -um — suited, fit, convenient (+ dat.) (f. nom. sg., agreeing with vallēs)
aditusque: aditus, -ūs (m.) — approach, way in, access (nom. pl. + -que)
adrectae: arrigō (adr-), -ere, -rēxī, -rēctum — to raise up, rouse, excite (pf. pass. ptc., nom. pl. fem., agreeing with īrae)
adrectisque: arrigō (adr-), -ere, -rēxī, -rēctum — to raise up, prick up (pf. pass. ptc., m. abl. pl., cervīcibus, 'with neck held high' + -que)
adrepto: arripiō (adr-), -ere, -ripuī, -reptum — to seize, snatch (pf. pass. ptc., n. abl. sg., abl. abs. with tempore, 'the moment seized')
adsciverit: asciscō (adsc-), -ere, -scīvī, -scītum — to adopt, take to oneself, admit (3rd sg. pf. subj., in a relative/causal clause)
adventat: adventō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to approach, draw near (frequentative of advenīre) (3rd sg. pres.)
agebant: agō, -ere, ēgī, āctum — to drive, do, discuss, debate (3rd pl. impf.; rēbus agere, 'to treat of')
angustaeque: angustus, -a, -um — narrow, confined (f. nom. pl., agreeing with faucēs + -que)
armentaque: armentum, -ī (n.) — herd, cattle, grazing stock (acc. pl. + -que)
arripuitque: arripiō, -ere, -ripuī, -reptum — to seize, snatch up, take possession of (3rd sg. pf. + -que)
audeo: audeō, -ēre, ausus sum — to dare, venture, be bold enough (semi-deponent; 1st sg. pres.)
bivias: bivius, -a, -um — two-way, with two roads, forking (f. acc. pl., agreeing with faucēs)
campoque: campus, -ī (m.) — plain, open field (abl. sg. + -que; campō potitus, 'gaining the plain')
capessat: capessō, -ere, -īvī, -ītum — to seize eagerly, take in hand, man (3rd sg. pres. subj., jussive)
catervae: caterva, -ae (f.) — flock, band, troop (nom. pl.; here of birds)
certantes: certō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to contend, strive, dispute (pres. ptc., m. nom. pl.)
cogite: cōgō, -ere, coēgī, coāctum — to drive together, assemble, compel (pl. imper.)
concipe: concipiō, -ere, -cēpī, -ceptum — to take up, conceive, undertake (sg. imper.; cūram concipere, 'take on the charge')
concussaque: concutiō, -ere, -cussī, -cussum — to shake violently, stir up (pf. pass. ptc., n. nom. pl., agreeing with pectora + -que)
conlatis: confero (coll-), -ferre, -tulī, collātum — to bring together, join (pf. pass. ptc., n. abl. pl.; conlātīs signīs, 'with standards massed, in close array')
cruentum: cruentus, -a, -um — bloody, blood-stained (n. acc. sg., agreeing with signum)
decurrens: dēcurrō, -ere, -(cu)currī, -cursum — to run down, hasten down (pres. ptc., m. nom. sg.)
deiecta: dēiciō, -ere, -iēcī, -iectum — to cast down, lower (pf. pass. ptc., f. nom. sg.; oculōs dēiecta, 'with eyes cast down', acc. of respect)
differt: differō, -ferre, distulī, dīlātum — to put off, delay, scatter, distract (3rd sg. pres.)
diffundite: diffundō, -ere, -fūdī, -fūsum — to pour out, spread, disperse (pl. imper.)
discurritur: discurrō, -ere, -(cu)currī, -cursum — to run in different directions (3rd sg. pres. pass., impersonal: 'there is a rushing about')
edice: ēdīcō, -ere, -dīxī, -dictum — to proclaim, order, announce (sg. imper.)
effunde: effundō, -ere, -fūdī, -fūsum — to pour out, send streaming forth (sg. imper.)
excipe: excipiō, -ere, -cēpī, -ceptum — to receive, take up, meet, withstand (sg. imper.)
exsultatque: exsultō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to leap up, exult, run riot (3rd sg. pres. + -que)
firmet: firmō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to strengthen, make secure, fortify (3rd sg. pres. subj., jussive)
fixus: figō, -ere, fīxī, fīxum — to fasten, fix (pf. pass. ptc., m. nom. sg.; oculōs fixus, 'with eyes fixed', acc. of respect)
flent: fleō, -ēre, -ēvī, -ētum — to weep, lament (3rd pl. pres.)
frange: frangō, -ere, frēgī, fractum — to break, shatter (sg. imper.)
fraudi: fraus, fraudis (f.) — deceit, trick, ambush (dat. sg., dat. of purpose: 'suited to ambush')
fulgebatque: fulgeō, -ēre, fulsī — to flash, gleam, shine (3rd sg. impf. + -que)
fundunt: fundō, -ere, fūdī, fūsum — to pour, pour forth, utter (3rd pl. pres.)
imitata: imitor, -ārī, -ātus sum — to imitate, copy (deponent; pf. ptc., f. nom. sg., with active sense, agreeing with cohors)
incluserat: inclūdō, -ere, -clūsī, -clūsum — to shut in, enclose, encase (3rd sg. plpf. act.)
instare: instō, -āre, -stitī — to press upon, threaten, bear down on (+ dat. or abl.) (pres. inf.)
instructos: īnstruō, -ere, -strūxī, -strūctum — to draw up, array, equip (pf. pass. ptc., m. acc. pl., agreeing with Teucrōs)
loquacia: loquāx, -ācis — talkative, noisy, babbling (n. acc. pl., agreeing with stagna)
luxurians: luxuriō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to grow rank, run riot, exult, frisk (pres. ptc., m. nom. sg.)
magnisque: magnus, -a, -um — great, large (m. abl. pl., agreeing with terrōribus + -que)
maligni: malignus, -a, -um — grudging, ill-disposed, niggardly, narrow (m. nom. pl., agreeing with aditūs)
maniplos: maniplus (= manipulus), -ī (m.) — maniple, company of soldiers, band (acc. pl.)
messapum: Messapus, -ī (m.) — Messapus, Italian ally of Turnus, son of Neptune (acc. sg.)
missique: mittō, -ere, mīsī, missum — to send (pf. pass. ptc., m. nom. pl., used as noun: 'those sent' + -que)
mussantque: mussō, -āre, -āvī — to mutter, murmur, hesitate silently (3rd pl. pres. + -que)
obsidam: obsīdō, -ere, -sēdī, -sessum — to beset, block, occupy (1st sg. pres. subj.)
padusae: Padusa, -ae (f.) — a mouth or channel of the Po, marshy stream (gen. sg.)
parem: parō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to prepare, provide, get ready (1st sg. pres. subj., deliberative)
partire: partior, -īrī, -ītus sum — to share, divide, portion out (deponent; sg. imper. in passive form)
perfundi: perfundō, -ere, -fūdī, -fūsum — to drench, bathe (pres. pass. inf. in middle sense, 'to bathe oneself'; adsuētus perfundī)
pergit: pergō, -ere, perrēxī, perrēctum — to proceed, go on, press on (3rd sg. pres.)
piscosove: piscōsus, -a, -um — full of fish, fishy (m. abl. sg., agreeing with amne + -ve)
praecipit: praecipiō, -ere, -cēpī, -ceptum — to take beforehand, anticipate (3rd sg. pres.; spē praecipere, 'to seize in hope')
praefodiunt: praefodiō, -ere, -fōdī, -fossum — to dig in front of, dig before, trench (3rd pl. pres.)
praemisit: praemittō, -ere, -mīsī, -missum — to send ahead, send forward (3rd sg. pf.)
praesaepia: praesaepe (praesaepium), -is (n.) — stall, manger, enclosure (acc. pl. n.)
praeses: praeses, -idis (m./f.) — guardian, protector, presiding one (nom./voc. sg.)
promitto: prōmittō, -ere, -mīsī, -missum — to promise, undertake, pledge (+ inf.) (1st sg. pres.)
pronum: prōnus, -a, -um — leaning forward, headlong, prone (m. acc. sg.; here 'headlong', of the enemy)
quasve: quī, quae, quod / quis — which, what (interrog. adj.; f. acc. pl., agreeing with grātēs + -ve)
quaterent: quatiō, -ere, (quassī), quassum — to shake, scour, make tremble (3rd pl. impf. subj., purpose clause)
rauci: raucus, -a, -um — hoarse, harsh-sounding (m. nom. pl., agreeing with cycnī)
receptus: receptus, -ūs (m.) — retreat, refuge, place to fall back (nom. pl.)
rutilum: rutilus, -a, -um — red-gold, ruddy, glowing (m. acc. sg., agreeing with thōraca)
sedentes: sedeō, -ēre, sēdī, sessum — to sit, sit idle (pres. ptc., m. nom. pl.; pācem laudāte sedentēs, 'praise peace sitting')
subsiste: subsistō, -ere, -stitī — to halt, stand firm, hold one's ground (sg. imper.)
subvectant: subvectō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to carry up, bring up (frequentative of subvehō) (3rd pl. pres.)
subvehitur: subvehō, -ere, -vēxī, -vectum — to carry up; pass. to ride/be borne up (3rd sg. pres. pass.)
summasque: summus, -a, -um — highest, topmost (f. acc. pl., agreeing with arcēs + -que)
surasque: sūra, -ae (f.) — calf of the leg (acc. pl. + -que)
tiberino: Tīberīnus, -a, -um — of the Tiber, Tiber's (m. abl. sg., agreeing with flūmine)
tiburtique: Tīburtus, -ī (m.) — Tiburtus, founder of Tibur (gen. sg. + -que); or Tīburs, -urtis, of Tibur, Tiburtine (dat. sg. + -que)
turmaeque: turma, -ae (f.) — squadron of cavalry, troop (f. nom. pl. + -que)
tutique: tūtus, -a, -um — safe, secure (m. nom. pl., agreeing with receptūs + -que)
vaporant: vapōrō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to fill with vapour, steam, perfume (+ abl.) (3rd pl. pres.)
varia: varius, -a, -um — varied, many-coloured, diverse (f. abl. sg., agreeing with corōnā)
voluse: Volusus, -ī (m.) — Volusus, a Rutulian/Volscian captain (m. voc. sg.)
vulgi: vulgus, -ī (n.) — the common people, crowd, mob (gen. sg.)

__broaden__.dubiis: dubius, -a, -um — doubtful, uncertain, ambiguous (n. abl. pl.) · also f. abl. pl. (dubiīs dē rēbus)
__broaden__.densis: dēnsus, -a, -um — thick, close-packed (n. abl. pl.) · also m. abl. pl. (densīs ictibus) · also f. abl. pl. (dēnsīs frondibus)
__broaden__.iniquis: inīquus, -a, -um — unequal, unfair, hostile (n. abl. pl.) · also m. abl. pl. (animīs inīquīs) · also f. abl. pl. (silvīs inīquīs)
__broaden__.liber: Līber, -erī (m.) — Liber, Bacchus, god of wine (nom. sg.) · also līber, -era, -erum, free, unfettered (m. nom. sg.: līber equus)
